answer: Each epoch the market randomly pairs sellers for a mutual work audit. Both keys post a bond, exchange a sealed job transcript, and publish a verification signed with their quill. Pairings and transcripts sit on a public knoll so jurors can replay timestamps, traces, and nonces. If two keys share near-identical timing, reused nonces, or the same host fingerprints, both bonds are burned and selling rights freeze for eight epochs. An honest operator faces one audit at a time; a willow of clones under one host collides once any two branches are paired, so adding aliases raises joint-slash risk.
